**Profile:** safe-wallet monorepo · TypeScript/React (Next.js web plus `packages/utils`) · Jest · tsc, eslint and prettier gates · stated rules come from AGENTS.md · security has little new surface

## What this review did not cover
- No tests or type-check were run (read-only review, as you asked). Every conclusion comes from reading the code.
- 5 of 8 findings (F4–F8) were not checked by paired agents.
- Mobile was not reviewed. It still uses the unchanged `detectSimilarAddresses`.
- The `.git/safe-code-review/last-run.tsv` record was not written, to keep this read-only.

## Fix before opening

**F2 · Bugs · P2 · CONFIRMED (both agents)**
`apps/web/src/components/common/TrustedSafesModal/ManageTrustedSafesContent.tsx:103`
- **What:** The row badge set is computed from `availableItems`, which is filtered by search. The confirm gate and Select-All exclusion in `useTrustedSafesModal.ts:113` are computed from the full `allSafes` list.
- **Failure:** A and B share their first 4 hex chars. The user searches for A, so B is filtered out. `detectListClusters([A])` returns early (`addressSimilarity.ts:148`), so A shows **no warning badge**, but clicking A still opens the similarity confirm dialog. Before this change the badge came from `similarityGroup` over the full list, so badge and gate agreed.
- **Also:** `availableItems` is rebuilt on every checkbox toggle, so both detectors rerun on every click.
- **Fix:** Return `flagged` (or `isAddressFlagged`) from `useTrustedSafesModal` and pass it through. Don't recompute it in the content component.

## Worth a ticket / fix soon

**F3 · Testing · P2 · CONFIRMED (both agents)**
`apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SelectSafesOnboarding/hooks/useOnboardingSafes.ts:41`
- **What:** New behaviour: a Safe added on any chain now pulls its owned and undeployed instances on every other chain into the trusted list, and out of owned.
- **Why it matters:** Only owned items get look-alike warnings, so the moved instances lose them.
- **Gap:** The existing test file is untouched and none of its 9 cases puts an address on two different chains. Reverting the change fails no test. `SelectSafesOnboarding.test.tsx` mocks the hook out entirely.
- **Add:** A test with an address added on chain 1 and owned on chain 137. Assert that it appears only in trusted, on both chains.

**F1 · Regression · P2 · CONTESTED (validator PARTIAL, refuter REFUTED); reworded**
`packages/utils/src/utils/addressSimilarity.ts:133` · `apps/web/src/features/address-poisoning/hooks/useSimilarityClusters.ts:25`
- **What:** On all five list surfaces, the within-list detector changed. It used to require a match on the first 4 **and** the last 4 hex chars. It now accepts either end **or** the other, and chains matches together (so A~B and B~C puts A and C in one group).
- **Scope:** This runs unconditionally for every user. Only the anchor half checks `ADDRESS_POISONING_PROTECTION`.
- **Agents:** Both agents showed the old detector was never flag-gated either, so my original "the flag was a kill switch" framing is withdrawn. The commit message says the change is intended.
- **What's left:** A 4-char match on either end is a 16-bit collision. A list of about 300 Safes has a rough 75% chance of at least one false cluster. Flagged Safes are left out of Select-All and need a confirm click, and chaining makes the groups grow.
- **Your call:** Keep it as a product decision, or put the OR rule behind the flag for rollout.

## Worth tidying (optional, no score impact)
1. Pull the repeated `useCallback((a) => flagged.has(a.toLowerCase()))` from `useTrustedSafesModal.ts:114` and `useManageNestedSafes.ts:75` into the result of `useSimilarityClusters` as `isFlagged`. About 6 lines.
2. Delete `getFlaggedSimilarAddressSet` and its tests (F6), or mark it deprecated if mobile might adopt it.

Reply "fix", "ticket" or "skip" for these. Doing nothing counts as skip.

## Not sure about these · Ruled out
- **Not sure:** `useOnboardingSafes.ts:47` removes duplicates across three sources with a case-sensitive `Set`. If the owned, undeployed and added lists ever disagree on checksum casing, the same Safe could appear twice. The old owned list already used this pattern, so it was not filed.
- **Not sure:** Anchor matches treat a one-end WARN like CRITICAL for gating. A large address book raises false flags. That half is behind the flag.
- **Ruled out:** Per-call cost of `getSimilarAddresses`. It is only called for the one pending confirmation.
- **Ruled out:** The union-find path compression in `detectListClusters` is correct.

## How this was produced
I scoped the diff myself and ran all nine category passes inline. F1–F3 each got a validator agent and a refuter agent. Outcome: **CONFIRMED 2 · CONTESTED 1 · REFUTED 0**. Nothing was posted, edited or run.
